title: Hebrews Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Hebrews 3: Jesus and Moses in the house, the call to hear his voice today, and the generation that did not enter into his rest.

questions.text: Who is named as the Apostle and High Priest of our confession?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 calls the holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, to consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession: Jesus.

questions.text: With whose faithfulness in all his house is he compared in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says he was faithful to him who appointed him, as Moses also was in all his house.

questions.text: Who has more honor, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because the one who built the house has more honor than the house.

questions.text: Who built all things, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says that every house is built by someone, but that the one who built all things is God.

questions.text: In what role was Moses faithful in all his house?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of the things that were afterward to be spoken.

questions.text: On what condition does the text say we are his house?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says Christ is faithful as a Son over his house, and that we are his house if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.

answers.text: If we keep the whole law
If we hold our confidence firm to the end
If we are counted among the fathers
If we have seen his deeds ourselves

questions.text: What are the hearers told not to do if they hear his voice today?
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 say, "Today if you will hear his voice, don't harden your hearts, as in the rebellion."

questions.text: For how long did the fathers see his deeds in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says that in the wilderness their fathers tested him and tried him, and saw his deeds for forty years.

questions.text: What did he swear in his wrath about that generation?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says, "As I swore in my wrath, 'They will not enter into my rest.'"

answers.text: That they would not enter his rest
That they would not see the land
That they would not hear his voice
That they would not keep his house

questions.text: Why were they not able to enter in, according to verse 19?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says we see that they were not able to enter in because of unbelief.
